_purpose: The designation-prefix convention QElectroTech actually uses, derived from the project's own hand-curated 10_electric/qet_labels.xml. This is the reference that the matching rules in keywords.json are calibrated against, and that tools/iec81346/score.py checks them with.
_provenance: Every entry whose 'evidenced_by' is non-empty comes from a category qet_labels.xml assigns that prefix to directly -- the curator's own decision, not an interpretation. Entries with an empty 'evidenced_by' are extrapolations by analogy, flagged so they can be challenged separately from the evidenced ones.
_relationship_to_iec_81346_2_2019: This is NOT the table in IEC 81346-2:2019. That edition classifies by abstract 'inherent function' and would call a sensor B and a switching contact Q, where this project uses P and S. It also treats L, V and Y as reserved, while this project uses all three (inductors, diodes, valves), and adds two-letter codes (EH, KF, RB, YB) that a single-letter scheme has no room for. What is used here is the classic DIN 40719 / IEC 60617-era electrical convention. An earlier version of this tooling was calibrated to the 2019 table and consequently contradicted the curated data on 62% of the categories both covered -- see the closed qelectrotech/qelectrotech-elements#69. Reconciling the two is a decision for the QET maintainers, not something to quietly encode here.

classes.note: Distinct from G: B is the generating or storing source itself, G is a mains-fed power supply unit.
Lighting as a load. An indicator lamp on a panel is signalling, so it is P, not EH.
A plain circuit breaker is F, but a magneto-thermal breaker, a disconnecting switch and an RCCB are Q -- the curated data draws that line explicitly.
The coil or device itself is K; its switching contacts are S.

A current transformer is L here, not T -- treated as an inductive sensing winding rather than a power transformer. (The folder name is misspelled 'tansformers' upstream; the elements inside are named correctly, which is what the rules end up matching on.)
Covers both 'tells the system something' (sensors, instruments) and 'tells the operator something' (lamps, buzzers, displays).
Switching a power circuit, as opposed to S, which is signal-level or manually operated switching.
A limit switch is S even though it sits under 390_sensors_instruments (which is P): the curated data overrides the parent, because the thing itself is a switch.
Not evidenced in qet_labels.xml -- extrapolated from the classic convention, where W is the standard letter for cabling. Treat proposals carrying W as less certain than the evidenced classes.
